title: introduce-synthetic-cohort-reteamer-and-subsequence-entropy-reporter
author: Maya Patel
description: Adds a new synthetic cohort re-teaming runner plus a subsequence-entropy reporter and an exporter pipeline. Motivation: previous workload runners treated user sessions as independent traces which lost signal about short-lived cohort affinity (sticky sequences that reappear within minutes). This PR implements a lightweight cohorting layer that can remap and coalesce request sequences into synthetic cohorts for more realistic load synthesis, and a downstream reporter that computes subsequence entropy across rolling windows to quantify stickiness. The description below covers design, tests, and usage. Design summary: 1) Reteamer: an offline + streaming runner that ingests sampled trace sessions, groups sequences by structural similarity (token-level n-gram overlap and KV-cache access patterns), and emits synthetic cohorted sequences with tunable churn parameters. The runner supports shuffling, prefix-preservation, and optional token-scrubbing for privacy. 2) Subsequence entropy reporter: sliding-window estimator that computes conditional entropy for variable-length subsequences and attributes entropy deltas to kernel-level execution buckets (via lightweight telemetry markers). This allows us to correlate sequence stickiness with kernel hotspots. 3) Exporter pipeline: compact parquet and newline-delimited JSON exporters with per-cohort statistics and per-kernel attribution lines for downstream visualization. Checklist: - [x] Runner implementation and CLI - [x] Entropy reporter algorithm and tests - [x] End-to-end DAG in benchmark pipelines - [x] Unit tests and integration tests - [x] Basic perf baseline in CI harness Commands and example run: benchlab run cohort-reteamer --input samples/session-sample.parquet --cohort-window 5m --churn 0.2 --output ./out/cohorts.parquet benchlab report subseq-entropy --input ./out/cohorts.parquet --window 60s --k-buckets 8 --output ./out/entropy.ndjson Backwards compatibility: defaults keep previous runner behavior when cohort-window is disabled. Privacy: token-scrubbing is enabled by default to avoid PII leakage. Related work: follows prototypes from ENG-2312 and extends ideas in ENG-2407 about session affinity modeling.

ci_checks: perf-baseline: pass (no regression within noise threshold)
perf_summary: Local synthetic runs (8x A100-ish nodes) show cohorted workload p95 increase of 3.1% vs uncoalesced baseline but end-to-end cost per useful token decreases by 6.8% due to improved batching and KV-cache reuse. Subsequence entropy reporter reveals two low-entropy cohorts responsible for 40% of identical prefix hits; kernel attribution maps those to a single attention kernel with elevated L2 miss ratio in our microbenchmarks.
release_notes: Add a new cohort re-teaming workload generator and a subsequence-entropy reporter for quantifying sequence stickiness and kernel-attributed hotspots. Useful for improved batching simulations and targeted kernel optimization.
